title: Isolation of Antigen-Specific Nanobodies Using MACS-Based Screening
author: Apisitt Thaiprayoon

materials: E. coli cells (New England Biolabs, catalog number: C2527H)
Competent NEB10β E. coli cells (New England Biolabs, catalog number: C3019H)
Saccharomyces cerevisiae strain BJ5465 (American Type Culture Collection, catalog number:

steps.title: Prepare Yglc4.5‑Trp medium
steps.instruction: Combine 20.6448 g sodium citrate, 6.7 g yeast nitrogen base (w/o amino acids), 20 g glucose, 3.8 g Drop‑out mix (‑Trp), and 10 mL 1× penicillin/streptomycin solution with water to a final volume of 1 L. Adjust pH to 4.5 with 1 N HCl and autoclave.

steps.title: Prepare Yglc‑Gal pH 6.0 medium
steps.instruction: Combine 6.7 g yeast nitrogen base (w/o amino acids), 20 g galactose, 3.8 g Drop‑out mix (‑Trp), and 10 mL 1× penicillin/streptomycin solution with water to 1 L. Adjust pH to 4.5 with 1 N HCl and autoclave.

steps.title: Prepare LB broth
steps.instruction: Dissolve 10 g peptone, 10 g yeast extract, and 5 g NaCl in water to 1 L. Adjust pH to 7.4 with 1 N HCl and autoclave.

steps.title: Prepare LB agar
steps.instruction: Add to LB broth 10 g peptone, 10 g yeast extract, 5 g NaCl, and 15 g agar per litre. Adjust pH to 7.4 with 1 N HCl and autoclave.

steps.title: Prepare chloramphenicol solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve 340 mg chloramphenicol in 10 mL absolute ethanol, filter‑sterilize (0.22 µm), aliquot 1 mL, store at –20 °C.

steps.title: Prepare kanamycin solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve 500 mg kanamycin in 10 mL water, filter‑sterilize (0.22 µm), aliquot 1 mL, store at –20 °C.

steps.title: Prepare carbenicillin solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve 1 g carbenicillin in 10 mL water, filter‑sterilize (0.22 µm), aliquot 1 mL into amber tubes, store at –20 °C.

steps.title: Prepare arabinose solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve 20 g arabinose in 100 mL water (20 % w/v), filter‑sterilize (0.22 µm), aliquot 1 mL, store at –20 °C.

steps.title: Prepare SOB medium
steps.instruction: Combine 20 g Bacto‑tryptone, 10 g yeast extract, 5 g NaCl, 0.186 g KCl, 2.4 g MgSO₄·7H₂O in water to 1 L, adjust pH to 7.4 with 1 N HCl, autoclave.

steps.title: Prepare PBS
steps.instruction: Dissolve 8 g NaCl, 0.2 g KCl, 1.44 g Na₂HPO₄, 0.245 g KH₂PO₄ in water to 1 L, adjust pH to 7.4 with 1 N HCl, autoclave.

steps.title: Prepare Western blot blocking buffer
steps.instruction: Combine PBS components (as above) with 50 g blotting‑grade blocker (5 % w/v) in 1 L water, adjust pH to 7.4 with 1 N HCl, autoclave.

steps.title: Prepare PBST
steps.instruction: Combine PBS components (as above) with 1 mL Tween‑20 (0.1 % v/v) in 1 L water, adjust pH to 7.4 with 1 N HCl, autoclave.

steps.title: Prepare 0.5 M Tris pH 6.8
steps.instruction: Dissolve 18.2 g Tris base in water to 100 mL, adjust pH to 6.8 with 1 N HCl, autoclave.

steps.title: Prepare 1.5 M Tris pH 8.8
steps.instruction: Dissolve 12.1 g Tris base in water to 100 mL, adjust pH to 8.8 with 1 N HCl, autoclave.

steps.title: Prepare 10 % SDS solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve 10 g SDS in water to 100 mL.

steps.title: Prepare 10 % APS solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve 10 g ammonium persulfate in water to 100 mL.

steps.title: Prepare 6× Laemmli buffer
steps.instruction: Mix 1 g SDS (10 % w/v), 10 mg bromophenol blue (0.01 % v/v), 5 mL glycerol (50 % w/v), 0.6 g Tris base (0.5 M), 1 mL β‑mercaptoethanol (10 % v/v) and water to 10 mL.

steps.title: Cast 12 % SDS‑PAGE gel
steps.instruction: To 8 mL total, combine 2.4 mL 40 % acrylamide/bis, 2 mL 1.5 M Tris pH 8.8, 80 µL 10 % SDS, 80 µL 10 % APS, 8 µL TEMED (0.1 % v/v), and water to volume.

steps.title: Cast 6 % SDS‑PAGE gel
steps.instruction: To 5 mL total, combine 0.75 mL 40 % acrylamide/bis, 1.25 mL 1.5 M Tris pH 8.8, 50 µL 10 % SDS, 50 µL 10 % APS, 5 µL TEMED (0.1 % v/v), and water to volume.

steps.title: Prepare 50× TAE buffer
steps.instruction: Dissolve 242.2 g Tris base (2 M), 57.1 mL glacial acetic acid (1 M), and 18.612 g EDTA (50 mM) in water to 1 L.

steps.title: Prepare cell lysis buffer
steps.instruction: Combine 8 g NaCl (0.137 M), 0.2 g KCl (2.7 mM), 1.44 g Na₂HPO₄ (10 mM), 0.245 g KH₂PO₄ (1.8 mM), and 10 g SDS (1 % w/v) in water to 1 L, adjust pH to 7.4 with 1 N HCl, autoclave.

steps.title: Prepare YPD agar
steps.instruction: Dissolve 10 g yeast extract, 20 g peptone, 20 g glucose, 15 g agar in water to 1 L, autoclave.

steps.title: Recover and scale up yeast library
steps.instruction: Thaw frozen yeast library aliquots on ice (≥5 × diversity; ≥2.5 × 10⁹ viable cells). Recover in a 2 L Erlenmeyer flask with 1 L Yglc4.5‑Trp, shake 200 rpm at 30 °C overnight. Optionally plate a small aliquot on YPD agar to assess diversity. Expand to three 2 L flasks (1 L each) under the same conditions for 48–72 h (OD₆₀₀ ≈ 10–30). Centrifuge cultures at 3,500 × g for 5 min, resuspend pellets in Yglc4.5‑Trp + 10 % DMSO to 1 × 10¹⁰ cells mL⁻¹, dispense 2 mL into cryovials and freeze at –80 °C using a controlled‑rate freezer.

steps.title: Induce surface Nb expression
steps.instruction: Thaw frozen library at 30 °C (≥5 × diversity; ≥2.5 × 10⁹ viable cells). Inoculate 1 L Yglc4.5‑Trp in a 2 L flask, incubate overnight at 30 °C, 200 rpm. Dilute at least ten‑fold above library diversity into Yglc‑Gal (pH 6.0) medium, ensuring ≥5 × 10⁹ cells are added. Incubate 25 °C, 200 rpm for 48 h to induce GAL1‑driven Nb display.

steps.title: Assess Nb expression by flow cytometry
steps.instruction: Measure OD₆₀₀ of induced culture (1 OD₆₀₀ ≈ 1.5 × 10⁷ cells mL⁻¹). Pipette 1 × 10⁶ cells into 500 µL PBS, centrifuge 3,500 × g 1 min at 4 °C. Aspirate supernatant, resuspend pellet in 100 µL fresh selection buffer. Add ~0.5 µg anti‑HA‑Alexa 647 (or 488) and 1 µM fluorescently labelled target protein to one tube; leave a second tube unstained as negative control. Rock 4 °C 15 min, centrifuge 3,500 × g 1 min 4 °C, discard supernatant, resuspend in 500 µL PBS, repeat wash once more. Finally resuspend in 100 µL PBS and analyse on a flow cytometer, using the unstained sample to set gates.

steps.title: Assess Nb expression by western blot
steps.instruction: Determine OD₆₀₀ and transfer ~1 × 10⁷ cells into 500 µL PBS (two tubes). Centrifuge 3,500 × g 1 min 4 °C, discard supernatant, resuspend each pellet in 100 µL PBS. Add 10 µg lyophilized zymolyase, incubate 30 °C water bath 1 h. Sonicate lysates, centrifuge 13,000 × g 10 min. Discard supernatant (cytoplasmic fraction); keep insoluble pellet, wash three times with PBS. Mix washed pellet with cell lysis buffer, centrifuge 13,000 × g 15 min. Collect supernatant, determine protein concentration (Bradford). Resuspend remaining insoluble pellet in 6× Laemmli buffer, heat 100 °C 5 min. Load 5 µg on a 10 % SDS‑PAGE, run electrophoresis, transfer to PVDF membrane. Probe with HRP‑anti‑HA (1:3000), develop with Clarity Max ECL, image on ChemiDoc XRS+.

steps.title: MACS‑based enrichment of antigen‑specific yeast
steps.instruction: Harvest 1 × 10⁸ induced yeast cells, centrifuge, resuspend in 1 mL sterile PBS, transfer to an EasySep™ separation tube. Add 1–2 µg biotinylated target antigen, incubate 37 °C, 200 rpm 20 min. Add EasySep™ isolation cocktail, incubate 37 °C, 200 rpm 20 min. Vortex RapidSpheres™ magnetic beads 1 min, add 40 µL beads per 1 mL sample, incubate 37 °C, 200 rpm 20 min. Top up to 2 mL with EasySep™ cell separation buffer, mix gently (2–3 pipette actions). Place tube in EasySep™ magnet 3 min at room temperature, then invert magnet and pour supernatant (enriched antigen‑specific yeast) into a new sterile tube.

steps.title: Biotinylate target protein
steps.instruction: Equilibrate EZ‑Link™ Sulfo‑NHS‑Biotin vial to room temperature. Dissolve 1–10 mg protein in 0.5–2 mL PBS. Calculate moles of protein, multiply by 20 to obtain moles of biotin required. Compute volume of 10 mM biotin solution to add using: µL = (mmol biotin × 443 g mmol⁻¹ × 500 µL) / 2.2 mg. Prepare 10 mM biotin by dissolving 2.2 mg in 500 µL ultrapure water. Add the calculated volume of biotin solution to the protein, mix gently, and incubate on ice 2 h (or at room temperature 30–60 min). Verify biotinylation by western blot using HRP‑streptavidin.

steps.title: Baseline growth for FLI‑TRAP screening
steps.instruction: Clone Ref8 Nb fragment into pDD18‑ssTorA‑GCN‑4‑FLAG (XbaI/SalI) and PCSK9‑CAT fragment into pDD322‑TatABC‑p17wt‑Bla (AvrII/NotI) to generate pDD18‑ssTorA‑Ref8Nb‑FLAG and pDD322‑TatABC‑CAT‑Bla. Transform both plasmids into E. coli MC4100 or NEB10β, plate on LB agar with 34 µg mL⁻¹ chloramphenicol and 50 µg mL⁻¹ kanamycin, incubate 37 °C overnight. Pick a single colony, inoculate 2 mL LB + antibiotics, grow 37 °C, 200 rpm overnight. Prepare LB agar plates containing a gradient of carbenicillin (≈12 µg mL⁻¹ to 1 mg mL⁻¹) combined with L‑arabinose at 0.1 %, 0.5 % and 1 % (w/v); also prepare control plates with arabinose only. Measure OD₆₀₀ of overnight culture, pellet, resuspend in fresh LB to OD₆₀₀ = 2.5. In a sterile 96‑well plate, make ten‑fold serial dilutions from 10⁻¹ to 10⁻⁶ (180 µL LB + 20 µL culture for first row). Spot 5 µL of each dilution onto each prepared plate using fresh tips, let spots dry, invert plates and incubate at 25 °C, 30 °C and 37 °C. Image plates after 24–48 h; record the carbenicillin/arabinose condition giving the highest background growth for later FLI‑TRAP experiments.

steps.title: FLI‑TRAP library transformation
steps.instruction: Electroporate ≥50 ng µL⁻¹ of the pDD18‑Nbs‑FLAG plasmid library into electro‑competent NEB10β cells (prepare five 50 µL aliquots, store –80 °C). Desalt 40 µL plasmid DNA on a 0.025 µm nitrocellulose membrane for 20 min while thawing cells on ice. Mix 30 µL DNA with each 50 µL cell aliquot in a 1‑mm cuvette, electroporate, then recover by washing three times with 1 mL pre‑warmed SOB. Transfer recovered cells to a 250 mL flask; repeat until the entire library is introduced. Incubate 37 °C, 200 rpm 1 h. Estimate transformants by diluting 20 µL culture into 180 µL SOB, performing five additional ten‑fold dilutions, plating 100 µL on LB + 34 µg mL⁻¹ chloramphenicol, counting colonies and calculating total transformants (target >2 × 10⁵).

steps.title: Co‑transform TatABC‑CAT‑Bla plasmid
steps.instruction: Thaw the NEB10β library cells (containing pDD18‑Nbs‑FLAG) on ice, mix with pDD322‑TatABC‑CAT‑Bla plasmid, electroporate in a 1‑mm cuvette, immediately add pre‑warmed SOB and incubate 37 °C, shaking to allow expression of the resistance marker. This co‑transformation yields cells harboring both plasmids for downstream FLI‑TRAP screening.

steps.title: FLI‑TRAP selection plates
steps.instruction: Prepare LB agar plates with the carbenicillin and L‑arabinose concentrations identified in the baseline growth step. Measure OD₆₀₀ of the co‑transformed culture, pellet, resuspend to OD₆₀₀ = 2.5 in fresh LB. Plate appropriate dilutions on the selection plates, incubate at the temperature giving the highest background growth (25 °C, 30 °C or 37 °C) for 24–48 h. Monitor colony appearance; colonies appearing within 16 h may be false positives. Pick multiple fast‑growing colonies, inoculate each into fresh LB with antibiotics, and incubate overnight at 25 °C for verification.

steps.title: Validate isolated clones
steps.instruction: Serially dilute each isolated clone and repeat the spot‑plating assay under the same carbenicillin/L‑arabinose conditions (steps from baseline growth). Include a parental plasmid control. Select clones showing higher carbenicillin resistance, extract plasmid DNA, and sequence the full‑length insert to confirm the presence of the intended Nb and absence of frameshifts. Re‑transform the verified plasmids into fresh E. coli (MC4100, NEB10β or BL21‑DE3), spot‑plate under identical selection conditions, and confirm that the phenotype (carbenicillin resistance) is plasmid‑dependent.

steps.title: Subclone and characterize Nbs
steps.instruction: Subclone selected Nb genes into pET28a expression vector, transform into an expression host, and induce protein production. Purify Nbs and assess by western blot (anti‑HA), SDS‑PAGE, ELISA (binding to PCSK9 wild‑type and D374Y mutant), and surface plasmon resonance for kinetic analysis. Record dose‑response curves and inhibition of PCSK9‑LDLR interaction as functional validation.
